51:1: Interpretation of Surat Adh-Dhariyat In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Shu`bah ibn al-Hajjaj narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Khalid ibn Ar`arah that he heard `Ali may God be pleased with him, and Shu`bah also on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl that he heard `Ali may God be pleased with him, and it was also confirmed from other chains of transmission on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, `Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, that he ascended the pulpit of Kufa and said: Do not ask me about a verse in the Book of God, nor about a Sunnah of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), except that I will inform you of it. Ibn al-Kawwa` stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is the meaning of the words of God, the Most High: And those who scatter [the winds] with scattering? `Ali may God be pleased with him said: The wind. He said: And those who carry burdens? `Ali may God be pleased with him said: The clouds. He said: And those who move easily? `Ali may God be pleased with him said: The ships. He said: And those who divide [their] command? `Ali may God be pleased with him said: The angels. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Hani’ narrated to us, Saeed ibn Salam al-Attar narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Subaygh al-Tamimi came to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the scatterers. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They are the winds, and had I not heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say it, I would not have said it. He said: Then tell me about the dividers. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They are the angels, and had I not heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say it, I would not have said it. He said: Then tell me about the sailors who run smoothly. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They are the ships, and had I not heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say it, I would not have said it. Then he ordered that he be flogged, so he was flogged a hundred times and put in a house. When he recovered, he called for him and flogged him a hundred times, put him on a saddlebag, and wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may God be pleased with him: Prevent people from sitting with him. He continued like that until he went to Abu Musa may God be pleased with him and swore solemn oaths that he did not find in himself what he had previously found in him. He wrote about that to 'Umar may God be pleased with him, and 'Umar wrote back: I think he has told the truth, so leave him alone and let him not sit with people. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah is weak, and Sa'id ibn Salam is not one of the hadith scholars. I said: "This hadith is weak and its chain of transmission is most likely to be attributed to 'Umar may God be pleased with him, because the story of Subaygh ibn 'Asal is well-known with 'Umar may God be pleased with him, and he only flogged him because he appeared to him to be stubborn and obstinate in what he asked about, and God knows best." Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned this story in a lengthy biography of Subaygh, and this is how it was interpreted by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them, and Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim did not narrate anything other than that. It has been said that what is meant by Al-Sharaiyat is the wind, as mentioned above, and by Al-Hamilat Waqra is the clouds, as mentioned above, because they carry water, as Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl said: I surrendered myself to the One to whom the rain clouds surrendered, carrying pure sweetness. As for the ones that run smoothly, what is well-known from the majority, as mentioned above, is that they are the ships, running smoothly in the water. Some of them said: They are the stars running smoothly in their orbits, so that this is a progression from the lowest to the highest to what is higher than it. So the winds are above them the clouds, and the stars are above them likewise, and the angels who divide a matter are above that, descending with the legal and cosmic commands of God. This is an oath from God Almighty on the occurrence of the Resurrection, and for this reason the Most High said: You are only promised a truth meaning a true report and the judgment which is the reckoning will surely come to pass meaning it will inevitably happen. Then God the Almighty said: {And the heaven full of textures} Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: full of beauty, splendor, goodness and smoothness. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Malik, Abu Salih, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Ar-Rabi bin Anas and others said. Ad-Dahhak, Al-Minhal bin Amr and others said: It is like the curly hair of water, sand and crops when the wind strikes them, so some of them weave themselves into others in many paths. That is the texture. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: Indeed, behind you is the liar, the misleader, and behind his head is texture, texture meaning curly hair. Abu Salih said: With texture is intensity. Khasif said: With texture is the one with impudence. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The heaven of the stars is woven with stars. Qatada said on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talha on the authority of Amr Al-Bakali on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, may God be pleased with them both: And the heaven of the stars means the seventh heaven. And it seems that he meant by that the heaven in which are the fixed stars, and according to many astronomers it is in the eighth heaven, which is above the seventh, and God knows best. All these sayings go back to one thing, which is beauty and splendor, as Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said. Because of its beauty, it is high, transparent, thick, strongly built, spacious, elegant in splendor, crowned with fixed and moving stars, decorated with the sun, the moon, and the planets. The Almighty said: Indeed, you are in a different statement. That is, you, O polytheists who denied the messengers, are in a different, disturbed statement that does not agree or come together. Qatada said: Indeed, you are in a different statement, between those who believe in the Qur'an and those who deny it. "He who is a liar will be turned away from it." That is, it is only promoted by those who are astray in themselves, because it is a false statement that only those who are led astray will be led astray because of it. He who is a liar, misguided, and ignorant of it will be turned away from it, as the Almighty said: "Indeed, you and what you worship * You will not be a deceiver for it * Except he who is destined for Hellfire." Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and As-Suddi said: "He who is a liar will be turned away from it." He who goes astray will be led astray from it. Mujahid said, "He who lies will be turned away from it" means he who is turned away from it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, "He who denies it will be turned away from this Qur'an. And the statement of God, the Most High, The liars will be destroyed. Mujahid said, The liars. He said, It is like the statement in 'Abasa, The man has been destroyed, how ungrateful he is. The liars are those who say, We will not be resurrected, and they do not have certainty. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, The liars will be destroyed, meaning the doubters will be cursed. This is what Muadh, may God be pleased with him, used to say in his sermon. The doubters are doomed. Qatadah said, The liars are the people of delusion and suspicion. And the statement of God, the Most High, Those who are in heedless confusion, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and others said, "In disbelief and doubt, they are heedless and distracted. "They ask, 'When is the Day of Judgment?'" They only say this out of denial, stubbornness, doubt, and rejection. God, the Most High, said, "The Day they will be tested over the Fire, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said, They will be tested and tormented." Mujahid said: Just as gold is tested by fire. Another group, such as Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Sufyan al-Thawri, said: They are tested and burn. Taste your trial. Mujahid said: Your burning. Another said: Your punishment. This is what you were hastening for. That is, this is said to them as a rebuke, a rebuke, a humiliation, and a disparagement. And God knows best.

This is what Muadh, may God be pleased with him, used to say in his sermon. The doubters are doomed. Qatadah said, The liars are the people of delusion and suspicion. And the statement of God, the Most High, Those who are in heedless confusion, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and others said, "In disbelief and doubt, they are heedless and distracted. "They ask, 'When is the Day of Judgment?'" They only say this out of denial, stubbornness, doubt, and rejection. God, the Most High, said, "The Day they will be tested over the Fire, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said, They will be tested and tormented." Mujahid said: Just as gold is tested by fire. Another group, such as Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Sufyan al-Thawri, said: They are tested and burn. Taste your trial. Mujahid said: Your burning. Another said: Your punishment. This is what you were hastening for. That is, this is said to them as a rebuke, a rebuke, a humiliation, and a disparagement. And God knows best.
51:14: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj said on the authority of Samak on the authority of Khalid ibn Arara that he heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Shu'bah also on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl that he heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, and it was also proven from other sources on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he ascended the pulpit of Kufa and said: Do not ask me about a verse in the Book of God Almighty, nor about a Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that I will inform you of it. Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is the meaning of the words of God Almighty: "And the scatterers with scatter" Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The wind. He said: "And those carrying burdens" He, may God be pleased with him, said: The clouds. He said: "And those running smoothly" He, may God be pleased with him, said: The ships. He said: "And those who divide a matter" He, may God be pleased with him, said: The angels. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Hani’ narrated to us, Saeed ibn Salam al-Attar narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Subaygh al-Tamimi came to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about the scatterers. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They are the winds, and had I not heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say it, I would not have said it. He said: Then tell me about the dividers. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They are the angels, and had I not heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say it, I would not have said it. He said: Then tell me about the sailors who run smoothly. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They are the ships, and had I not heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say it, I would not have said it. Then he ordered that he be flogged, so he was flogged a hundred times and put in a house. When he recovered, he called for him and flogged him a hundred times, put him on a saddlebag, and wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may God be pleased with him: "Prevent people from sitting with him." He continued like that until he went to Abu Musa may God be pleased with him and swore solemn oaths that he did not find in himself what he had previously found in him. He wrote about that to 'Umar may God be pleased with him, and 'Umar wrote back: "I think he has told the truth, so leave him alone and let him not sit with people." Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: "Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah is weak, and Sa'id ibn Salam is not one of the hadith scholars." I said: "This hadith is weak and its chain of transmission is most likely to be attributed to 'Umar may God be pleased with him, because the story of Subaygh ibn 'Asal is well-known with 'Umar may God be pleased with him, and he only flogged him because he appeared to him to be stubborn and obstinate in what he asked about, and God knows best." Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned this story in a lengthy biography of Subaygh, and this is how it was interpreted by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them, and Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim did not narrate anything other than that. It has been said that what is meant by Al-Sharaiyat is the wind, as mentioned above, and by Al-Hamilat Waqra is the clouds, as mentioned above, because they carry water, as Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl said: I surrendered myself to the One to whom the rain clouds surrendered, carrying pure sweetness. As for the ones that run smoothly, what is well-known from the majority, as mentioned above, is that they are the ships, running smoothly in the water. Some of them said: They are the stars running smoothly in their orbits, so that this is a progression from the lowest to the highest to what is higher than it. So the winds are above them the clouds, and the stars are above them likewise, and the angels who divide a matter are above that, descending with the legal and cosmic commands of God. This is an oath from God Almighty on the occurrence of the Resurrection, and for this reason the Most High said: You are only promised a truth meaning a true report and the judgment which is the reckoning will surely come to pass meaning it will inevitably happen. Then God the Almighty said: {And the heaven full of textures} Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: full of beauty, splendor, goodness and smoothness. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Malik, Abu Salih, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Ar-Rabi bin Anas and others said. Ad-Dahhak, Al-Minhal bin Amr and others said: It is like the curly hair of water, sand and crops when the wind strikes them, so some of them weave themselves into others in many paths. That is the texture. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: Indeed, behind you is the liar, the misleader, and behind his head is texture, texture meaning curly hair. Abu Salih said: With texture is intensity. Khasif said: With texture is the one with impudence. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The heaven of the stars is woven with stars. Qatada said on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talha on the authority of Amr Al-Bakali on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, may God be pleased with them both: And the heaven of the stars means the seventh heaven. And it seems that he meant by that the heaven in which are the fixed stars, and according to many astronomers it is in the eighth heaven, which is above the seventh, and God knows best. All these sayings go back to one thing, which is beauty and splendor, as Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said. Because of its beauty, it is high, transparent, thick, strongly built, spacious, elegant in splendor, crowned with fixed and moving stars, decorated with the sun, the moon, and the planets. The Almighty said: "Indeed, you are in a different statement." That is, you, O polytheists who denied the messengers, are in a different, disturbed statement that does not agree or come together. Qatada said: "Indeed, you are in a different statement, between those who believe in the Qur'an and those who deny it. He who is a liar will be turned away from it." That is, it is only promoted by those who are astray in themselves, because it is a false statement that only those who are led astray will be led astray because of it. He who is a liar, misguided, and ignorant of it will be turned away from it, as the Almighty said: "Indeed, you and what you worship * You will not be a deceiver for it * Except he who is destined for Hellfire." Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and As-Suddi said: "He who is a liar will be turned away from it." He who goes astray will be led astray from it. Mujahid said, "He who lies will be turned away from it" means he who is turned away from it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, "He who denies it will be turned away from this Qur'an. And the statement of God, the Most High, The liars will be destroyed. Mujahid said, The liars. He said, It is like the statement in 'Abasa, The man has been destroyed, how ungrateful he is. The liars are those who say, We will not be resurrected, and they do not have certainty. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, The liars will be destroyed, meaning the doubters will be cursed. This is what Muadh, may God be pleased with him, used to say in his sermon. The doubters are doomed. Qatadah said, The liars are the people of delusion and suspicion. And the statement of God, the Most High, Those who are in heedless confusion, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and others said, "In disbelief and doubt, they are heedless and distracted. "They ask, 'When is the Day of Judgment?'" They only say this out of denial, stubbornness, doubt, and rejection. God, the Most High, said, "The Day they will be tested over the Fire, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said, They will be tested and tormented." Mujahid said: Just as gold is tested by fire. Another group, such as Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Sufyan al-Thawri, said: They are tested and burn. Taste your trial. Mujahid said: Your burning. Another said: Your punishment. This is what you were hastening for. That is, this is said to them as a rebuke, a rebuke, a humiliation, and a disparagement. And God knows best.
51:15: God the Almighty says, informing us about those who fear God the Almighty that on the Day of Resurrection they will be in gardens and springs, unlike the torment, humiliation, burning, and shackles that those wretched ones will be in. God the Almighty says: Taking what their Lord has given them. Ibn Jarir said: meaning, doing what God has given them of the obligatory duties. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. That is, before the obligatory duties were imposed on them, they were also doers of good in their deeds. Then it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Hamid, who said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Umar, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding God the Almighty's statement: Taking what their Lord has given them, he said: of the obligatory duties. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. He said: before the obligatory duties were imposed on them, they did good. This chain of narration is weak and is not authentic from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. It was narrated by Uthman bin Abi Shaybah on the authority of Muawiyah bin Hisham on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Omar Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned it. What Ibn Jarir interpreted with it is questionable, because the words of God Almighty, taking are a condition of His words in gardens and springs. So the righteous, while they are in gardens and springs, are taking what their Lord has given them, meaning of bliss, joy, and happiness. And the words of God Almighty: Indeed, they were before that meaning in this worldly abode doers of good are like His words, may He be glorified and exalted: Eat and drink in pleasure for what you put forth in the days gone by. Then God Almighty explained their good deeds, saying, may He be glorified and exalted: They slept but little of the night. The commentators differed on that with two opinions: One of them that ma is a negative, meaning they did not sleep but little of the night. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Not a night would pass for them without them taking from it, even a little. Qatada said on the authority of Mutraf Ibn Abdullah: Say: A night does not come upon them except that they pray to God, the Almighty, either from the beginning or from the middle. Mujahid said: Say: They do not sleep at night until morning without praying at night. Qatada said the same. Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him and Abu Al-Aliyah said: They used to pray between Maghrib and Isha. Abu Ja`far Al-Baqir said: They used to not sleep until they prayed the Isha prayer. The second statement is that ma is a source meaning they used to sleep and slumber for a short time at night. Ibn Jarir chose this. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, They used to sleep but little of the night, meaning they struggled with standing at night and would only sleep a little. They became active and continued until dawn, until they used to seek forgiveness at dawn. Qatada said, Al-Ahnaf bin Qais said, They used to sleep but little of the night, meaning they would only sleep a little, then he would say, You are not of the people of this verse. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, Al-Ahnaf bin Qais used to say, “I showed my deeds to the deeds of the people of Paradise, and behold, there were some people who were far removed from us, some whose deeds we could not reach, they used to sleep but little of the night. I showed my deeds to the deeds of the people of Hellfire, and behold, there were some people in whom there was no good, who denied the Book of God and His Messengers, who denied the resurrection after death. I found among our best the status of a people who mixed good deeds with bad.” Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: A man from Banu Tamim said to my father: O Abu Usamah, I do not find a description among us. God mentioned a people and said: They used to sleep but little of the night, but by God, we do not get up but little of the night. My father may God be pleased with him said to him: Blessed is he who sleeps when he feels drowsy and fears God when he wakes up. Abdullah bin Salam may God be pleased with him said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, the people rushed to him, and I was among those who rushed. When I saw his face (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing I heard him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say was: “O people, feed the poor, uphold the ties of kinship, spread peace, and pray at night when people are asleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace.” Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Huyayy ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Indeed, in Paradise there are rooms whose outside can be seen from their inside and whose inside can be seen from their outside. Abu Musa al-Ash’ari may God be pleased with him said: For whom are they, O Messenger of God? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: For those who speak gently, feed the poor, and stand in prayer for God while people are asleep. Muammar said regarding the verse: {They used to sleep but little of the night} Az-Zuhri and Al-Hasan used to say: They used to pray most of the night. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and Ibrahim An-Nakha’i said: {They used to sleep but little of the night} they did not sleep. Ad-Dahhak said: “Indeed, before that, they were doers of good. They were few.” Then he began by saying: {They used to sleep but little of the night. And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness.} This statement is far-fetched and arbitrary. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And in the hours before dawn they seek forgiveness} Mujahid and others said: They pray. Others said: They performed the night prayer and delayed seeking forgiveness until the hours before dawn, as God the Almighty said: {And those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn}. If seeking forgiveness is during prayer, then it is better. It has been proven in the Sahihs and other books on the authority of a group of the Companions may God be pleased with them, on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said: “God the Almighty descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: Is there anyone who repents, that I may accept his repentance? Is there anyone who seeks forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone who asks, that his request may be granted? Until dawn breaks.” Many commentators said regarding the words of God the Almighty, informing about Jacob that he said to his sons, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, they said: He delayed them until the time of dawn. God the Almighty said: And in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived. After describing them with prayer, He followed up with describing them with zakat, righteousness, and kinship, saying: And in their wealth is a right. That is, a divided portion that they have set aside for the beggar and the deprived. As for the beggar, he is well-known and he is the one who initiates the begging, and he has a right, as Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’ and Abdur-Rahman, they said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mus’ab ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Abi Yahya, on the authority of Fatimah bint al-Husayn, on the authority of her father al-Husayn ibn Ali may God be pleased with them both, he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The beggar has a right, even if he comes on a horse. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with this same chain of transmission. Then he attributed it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, and it was narrated from the hadith of Al-Harmas ibn Ziyad with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). As for the Mahram, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and Mujahid said: He is the one who has no share in Islam, meaning he has no share in the public treasury, nor does he earn or make a living from it. The Mother of the Believers Aisha may God be pleased with her said: He is the one who can hardly earn his living. Ad-Dahhak said: He is the one who has no wealth except that it is lost, and God has decreed that for him. Abu Qilabah said: A flood came to Yamamah and took away a man’s wealth, so a man from among the Companions may God be pleased with them said: This is the Mahram. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both also said, as did Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Ibrahim An-Nakha’i, Nafi’ the freed slave of Ibn ‘Umar may God be pleased with them both, and ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah: The Mahram is the one who has lost his share. Qatadah and Az-Zuhri said: The Mahram is the one who does not ask people for anything. Az-Zuhri said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The poor is not the one who travels around and is sent away by a morsel or two, or a date or two, but the poor is the one who does not find enough wealth to make him independent and is not noticed so that charity may be given to him.” This hadith was also narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs from another chain of narration. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: He is the one who comes after the spoils of war have been divided and is given alms. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: One of our companions told me: We were with ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz may God be pleased with him on the road to Mecca, and a dog came. ‘Umar may God be pleased with him snatched a sheep’s shoulder and threw it at him, saying: They say he is the one who is deprived. Al-Sha’bi said: I am unable to know who is the one who is deprived. Ibn Jarir preferred that the deprived is the one who has no money for any reason and his money has been lost, whether he is unable to earn a living or his money or the like has been destroyed by a calamity or the like. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Qais bin Muslim on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a detachment and they captured spoils. Then some people came to him who had not witnessed the spoils, so this verse was revealed: And in their wealth is a right for the needy and the deprived. This necessitates that this was revealed in Medina, but it is not so. Rather, it is Meccan and includes what follows it. And the Almighty’s saying: And on the earth are signs for those of certainty means that there are signs in it that indicate the greatness of its Creator and His dazzling power, in what He has created in it of various types of plants, animals, pastures, mountains, deserts, rivers and seas, and the difference in people’s languages and colors and what they were created with of wills and powers, and what they have between them of disparity in minds, understandings, movements, happiness and misery, and what is in their composition of wisdom in placing each of their limbs in the place where it is needed. For this reason, the Almighty said: And in yourselves, then will you not see? Qatadah said: Whoever contemplates the creation of himself will know that he was created and his joints were made flexible for worship. Then God the Almighty said: And in the sky is your provision meaning rain and that which you are promised meaning Paradise. This was stated by Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Mujahid and others. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Wasil al-Ahadab recited this verse: And in the sky is your provision and that which you are promised and said: Do I not see my provision in the sky and I seek it on earth? So he entered a ruin and stayed for three days without finding anything. On the third day, he saw a hole in the date palm. He had a brother who was better-intentioned than him. He entered with him, and they became two holes. This was their habit until death separated them. God Almighty said: By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth, just as you speak. God Almighty swears by His noble self that what He promised them regarding the Resurrection, the Rising, and the Recompense will inevitably happen. It is the truth, there is no doubt about it, so do not doubt it, just as you do not doubt your speech when you speak. Whenever Muadh, may God be pleased with him, narrated something, he would say to his companion: This is the truth, just as you are here. Musaddad said, on the authority of Ibn Abi Udayy, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: It reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God fight people to whom their Lord swore, but they did not believe. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Udayy, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and he mentioned it as a mursal.

It is the truth, there is no doubt about it, so do not doubt it, just as you do not doubt your speech when you speak. 51:24: This story was mentioned in Surat Hud and Surat Al-Hijr as well. His saying: Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Abraham? means those for whom honor was reserved. Imam Ahmad and a group of scholars held that hospitality is obligatory for the guest, and the Sunnah has mentioned this as is apparent in the revelation. And the Almighty’s saying: “They said, ‘Peace.’ He said, ‘Peace.’” The nominative is stronger and more firmly established than the accusative, so returning it is better than taslim. That is why the Almighty said: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or at least return it equally. So Al-Khalil chose the best. And the Almighty’s saying: A people of unknown standing is that the angels, namely Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, came to him in the form of handsome young men who were greatly awe-inspiring. That is why He said: A people of unknown standing. And the Almighty’s saying: So he turned to his family means he slipped away quickly and secretly. And brought a fattened calf means from the best of his wealth. And in the other verse: And he did not delay in bringing a roasted calf meaning roasted on embers. And brought it near to them means he brought it close to them. He said, ‘Will you not eat?’ He was gentle in his expression and presented it well. This verse organized the etiquette of hospitality, for he brought food from a place they did not notice, quickly. He did not show them favors first, saying, We will bring you food, but rather he brought it quickly and secretly. He brought the best of what he found of his wealth, which was a young, fat, roasted calf. So he brought it near to them. He did not place it and say, Come near. Rather, he placed it in their hands and did not command them in a manner that would be difficult for the listener to hear, in a definitive manner. Rather, he said, Will you not eat? as a way of offering and being kind, as the speaker says today: If you see that you should be generous, do good, and give charity, then do so. And the Almighty’s saying: So he felt fear of them This is impossible based on what was mentioned previously in the story in the other surah, which is the Almighty’s saying: “But when he saw that their hands did not reach him, he disapproved of them and felt fear of them. They said, “Do not fear. Indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lot, * And his wife was standing there.” So she laughed.” That is, she was pleased with their destruction for their rebellion and defiance of God Almighty. At that time, the angels gave her the good report of Isaac and, after Isaac, Jacob. “She said, ‘Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and my husband an old man? Indeed, this is a strange thing.’ They said, ‘Do you wonder at the command of God? The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.’” For this reason, God Almighty said here: And give him good tidings of a knowledgeable boy. The good report for him is good report for her, because the child is from them, so each of them has the good report of him. God the Almighty said: Then his wife came with a shriek meaning with a great scream and wailing. This was said by Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Salih, Ad-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, Ath-Thawri, and As-Suddi. It is her saying, Woe to me! “And she slapped her face” meaning she struck her forehead with her hand. This was said by Mujahid and Ibn Sabit. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both said: She slapped her face meaning in amazement, as women are amazed by a strange matter. And a barren old woman said meaning, how can I give birth when I am old, when I was barren in my youth and could not conceive? “They said, ‘Thus says your Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Wise, the Knowing’” meaning, He is All-Knowing of the honor you deserve, Wise in His words and deeds.

51:52: God the Almighty says, consoling His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “And just as these polytheists said to you, the first deniers said to their messengers: “Likewise, there came not to those before them a messenger but they said, ‘A magician or a madman.’” God the Almighty says: Do they enjoin one another to do so? That is, did they enjoin this statement upon one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people. That is, they are a transgressing people whose hearts are alike, so the later ones among them said as the earlier ones did. God the Almighty says: So turn away from them, that is, turn away from them, O Muhammad, for you are not to be blamed. That is, we do not blame you for that. And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers. That is, only the believing hearts benefit from it. Then the Almighty says: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. That is, I only created them to command them to worship Me, not because I need them. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except to worship Me. That is, except that they acknowledge My worship willingly or unwillingly. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jurayj said: Except that they may be known. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Except that they may worship, meaning, Except for worship. Al-Suddi said: Some forms of worship are beneficial and some are not beneficial. “And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’” This is worship on their part, and it does not benefit them with polytheism. Al-Dahhak said: What is meant by this are the believers. God the Almighty said: “I do not desire from them any provision, nor do I desire that they feed them. Indeed, it is God who is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy.” Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam and Abu Saeed narrated to us: Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited to me: Indeed, it is God who is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Isra’il. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. The meaning of the verse is that God the Blessed and Exalted created His servants to worship Him alone, with no partner or associate. Abu Mu'awiyah said: He is fixing something, so we helped him with it. When he finished, he supplicated for us and said: Do not despair of provision as long as your heads are shaking, for a person is born red with no scale on him, then God gives him provision.
